prerequisites: It is recommended to have previously passed the subjects "Mathematical Fundamentals of Engineering" and "Physical Fundamentals of Engineering".
It would also be desirable for students to have basic knowledge of computer science, programming, and languages.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have acquired fundamental knowledge of the laws governing fluid behavior, enabling them to understand and address real engineering problems in various fields of application.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and its application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.

syllabus_topics: Equilibrium of floating and submerged bodies
Physical meaning of dimensionless numbers: Reynolds, Euler, Froude, Mach
BUCKINGHAM's Theorem: drainage through orifices, friction in uniform conduits, drainage over open works, singular energy losses
Description of fluid motion. Euler and Lagrange methods
Fluid dynamics equations: Navier-Stokes and Euler equations
One-dimensional method for fluid flow analysis
Head loss in pipes. DARCY-WEISBACH equation
Friction equations in pipes. MOODY diagram
Effective energy head of a turbomachine
Operating point. Pumping systems: Simple and Complex
Complex systems. Series and parallel pipe connection
Types of networks: branched and meshed
Uniform flows. Chezy and Manning equations
Closed open channels. Drainage and sanitation pipes
Flow measurement in forced channels: venturimeter, orifice, Pitot tube, propeller or current meter flowmeters, ultrasonic and electromagnetic flowmeters
Flow measurement in open channels: discharge under gates, thin-wall weirs, modular flowmeters, current meters, ultrasonic flowmeters, tracers, etc.
Experimental Practice 2. Head Losses in Forced Flows
Experimental Practice 3. Flow Measurement in Forced Flows
Experimental Practice 4. Flow Measurement in Open Channels
assessment_rules: The evaluation is based on continuous assessment (40% of the final grade) and a final exam (60%). Continuous assessment includes practical reports (5%), a practical test (10%), and a theory test (25%). The final exam consists of problem-solving. A minimum score of 3 is required in the problem-solving exam; otherwise, the final grade will be only the score from this exam. A minimum final grade of 5 is required to pass the course. Alternatively, students can opt for a single final evaluation (100% of the grade), comprising a problem part (60%) and a theory part (40%), which replaces all continuous assessment scores. For the extraordinary call, continuous assessment scores are retained, or students can opt for the single final evaluation under the same conditions as the ordinary call.
